deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the manuscript of Riemann's posthumously published memoir 'Ueber die Fläche vom kleinsten Inhalt bei gegebener Begrenzung' (Abh. Ges. Wiss. Göttingen 13, 1867, edited by Hattendorff). The page belongs to the doubly-connected case: a minimal surface bounded by two closed polygons lying in parallel planes.

Setup carried over from the previous page:
- The annular surface is mapped conformally onto a two-sheeted Riemann surface T over the t-plane, branched at t = ±i and t = ±i/κ. This is an elliptic curve with Δ(t)^2 = (1+t^2)(1+κ^2 t^2).
- The Gauss-map variable η (stereographic image of the normal) satisfies d log η/dt = φ(t,Δ)/Δ(t), where φ is rational in t and Δ.
- φ has simple zeros at the points c, c' (the non-zero, finite corners C, C' of the η-image H). It has simple poles at the points b, b' (the corners of H at η = 0 or ∞).
- The previous page counts 4m free real constants. These are 4m−2 of the points (the Abel relation fixes one, and one may be chosen freely), the modulus κ, and a real factor in φ. On this page the general count is 2n+2m, consistent with the two polygons having n and m vertices.

(1) Period conditions. Let γ be a closed curve on T enclosing the branch points i and i/κ, i.e. a curve going once around the annulus. η must be single-valued on the annulus. Its Gauss image must also wind exactly once around the origin, because the horizontal normal of a surface between parallel planes turns once around the core. Hence
- Re ∮_γ φ dt/Δ = 0 (|η| returns to its value), and
- Im ∮_γ φ dt/Δ = 2π, i.e. the period equals 2πi (the argument of η increases by 2π).
These are two real conditions, leaving 2n+2m−2 constants.

(2) Corner conditions. Requiring η(c) = C and η(c') = C' for the prescribed corners of the η-image gives, by Riemann's count, an equal number 2n+2m−2 of conditions. On the next page the moduli |C|, |C'| are then treated as n+m−2 free parameters, subject to two further closing conditions.

(3) The coordinate normal to the planes. Choose the x-axis perpendicular to both boundary planes. X = x + i x*, with x* the harmonic conjugate of x in the conformal structure. Cut the annulus by a transversal joining the two boundaries, making it simply connected, so that X is single-valued on it.
- Re X = x is constant on each boundary (0 and h) and on each level curve, which are the sections by parallel planes.
- Along each level curve Im X increases monotonically. Going once around, it increases by the same constant, namely the period of x*, which is the flux of ∇x.
- Hence X maps the cut surface one-to-one onto a 'parallelogram'. Its two sides Re X = 0 and Re X = h correspond to the boundaries and are parallel to the imaginary axis. Its other two sides, the images of the two banks of the cut, may be curved but are translates of each other by i·(period).
- Implicit step (mine): monotonicity holds because x is a harmonic function on a doubly connected domain with constant boundary values (a multiple of harmonic measure), so it has no critical points. Its level curves are therefore simple closed curves homotopic to the core.

(4) Statement of the next step. This parallelogram must be mapped conformally onto the upper half T1 of T, carrying its vertical sides to the two boundary curves and the other sides to the banks of a cut in T. The next page realizes this by X = iC∫dt/Δ + C', with h = 2C∫_0^i i dt/Δ, which is a complete elliptic integral.
errors: The previous page states 4m free constants (using m for both boundaries), while this page speaks of 2n+2m−2 remaining after two conditions. The notation is inconsistent across pages, but the count is consistent if the two polygons have n and m vertices respectively.

The claim that the corner conditions η(c)=C, η(c')=C' furnish exactly 2n+2m−2 independent real conditions is asserted, not justified. Two real conditions per corner give 2n+2m, and the reduction by 2 (presumably global rotation/scaling or a dependence on the period conditions) is left implicit. The next page then re-frees n+m−2 moduli, so the count is heuristic in the style of the period.
The monotonic growth of Im X along level curves (absence of critical points of x) is asserted without proof. It is true, but it is an unstated step.
Calling the image a 'Parallelogramm' when two sides may be curved is loose terminology. Riemann himself immediately qualifies it.

results.what: Period conditions on d log η: Re of the period around the cycle through i, i/κ is 0 and Im equals 2π (Gauss map winds once around the annulus)
results.modern_name: Period/closing conditions for the logarithmic derivative of the Gauss map on an annulus (Weierstrass–Enneper data on a torus-type double)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (posthumous memoir 1867); Weierstrass 1866 for the representation in general

results.what: Parameter count of the Plateau problem for two polygons in parallel planes (constants vs conditions)
results.modern_name: Dimension count / moduli count for polygonal Plateau problem (Riemann–Schwarz method)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann 1867 (published by Hattendorff); later Schwarz, Garnier

results.what: Conformal image of the cut annulus under X = x + i x*: a strip-parallelogram with vertical sides Re X=0, h and translation-congruent cut sides
results.modern_name: Conformal modulus of a doubly connected domain via harmonic measure; uniformization of the annulus to a cylinder
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (mapping theorem ideas, 1851/1857), here applied in the minimal-surface memoir 1867

deep.surprise_reason: This page is the manuscript of a section of Riemann's posthumously published minimal-surface memoir (Hattendorff 1867, Werke). The content (period conditions, constant count, mapping by X to a parallelogram) is known to be his and is routine within that published work.

checkable.asserts: Substitution t = i s turns dt/Δ(t) into i ds/sqrt((1-s^2)(1-k^2 s^2)), so ∫_0^i dt/Δ = i·K(k^2) and h = 2C∫_0^i i dt/Δ = -2C·K.
Numerical check that the half-period ∫_0^1 ds/sqrt((1-s^2)(1-k^2 s^2)) equals elliptic_k(k^2) (sympy parameter m=k^2), here for k=1/2; the result should be ≈0.
In a round annulus 1<r<R, x = h log r / log R is harmonic with x=0 and x=h on the boundaries (model of the coordinate normal to the planes); the result is 0.

X = h log w / log R has constant real part on circles and imaginary part increasing by the constant 2πh/log R once around, so the cut annulus maps to a rectangle with sides parallel to the imaginary axis.
Δ(t)^2 has real coefficients, so Δ is real-symmetric: conjugate t gives conjugate values, consistent with φ being real on the real axis.

transcription_corrections: Lines 9–10: the inserted word before 'die 2n+2m−2' appears to be 'Für' with 'die' written above; the image reads roughly 'haben soll. Für die 2n+2m−2 übrig bleibenden Constanten'. The crossed-out words are 'genügen, aus der / den Punkten'.
In 'daß den Punkten [-..-] c, c'' a short struck-through symbol precedes c (possibly a 'b' or 'c'). It is illegible but irrelevant.
The marginal folio number '42' on the right edge belongs to the archive foliation, not the text.
'die gegebenen Punkte C, C' in der η-Ebene' is correct as transcribed (here C, C' denote corners in the η-plane, distinct from the integration constants C, C' on the next page).
